source.text: Πρωῒ δὲ ἐπανάγων εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἐπείνασεν.

records.literal_gloss: Early then returning into the city he was hungry.

en.L: Now early in the morning, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was returning to the city, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was hungry.
en.B: Early in the morning, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going back into the city, Jesus felt hungry.
en.R: Early the next morning, Jesus was going back to the city. He was hungry.

decisions.choice: early: in the early morning, before full daylight
decisions.reason: The word is used of the last part of the night and the first hours of day.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν μίαν ἐπὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἦλθεν ἐπ’ αὐτήν, καὶ οὐδὲν εὗρεν ἐν αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ φύλλα μόνον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ· Μηκέτι ἐκ σοῦ καρπὸς γένηται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· καὶ ἐξηράνθη παραχρῆμα ἡ συκῆ.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen fig tree one by the road he came to it, and nothing found on it if not leaves only, and he says to it, No longer from you fruit may be into the age. And withered immediately the fig tree.

en.L: And seeing a single fig tree by the road, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to it and found nothing on it except leaves only, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to it, "May fruit no longer come from you, forever." And the fig tree withered at once.
en.B: Seeing a fig tree beside the road, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up to it, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found nothing on it except leaves. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to it, "From now on, may no fruit ever grow on you!" At once the fig tree dried up.
en.R: Jesus saw a fig tree beside the road. He went to it to find some figs, but there was nothing on it except leaves. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the tree, "No fruit will ever grow on you again!" Right away the fig tree dried up.

decisions.choice: nothing but leaves: a tree in leaf that promised fruit and had none
alternatives: a tree out of season with no promise of fruit
decisions.reason: Fig trees put out small early figs with their leaves in spring. A tree full of leaves but bare of these had nothing to give.

decisions.choice: the withering: an acted sign of judgment on a fruitless people
alternatives: an act of anger at the tree
decisions.reason: The prophets picture Israel as a fig tree that God finds without fruit (Jeremiah 8:13; Micah 7:1). Matthew places the sign beside the temple scene and the parables about fruit (21:34, 41, 43).

decisions.choice: one: a single tree standing alone
decisions.reason: The word can mean only "a", but it may point to one tree by itself along the road.

decisions.choice: may no fruit come from you: a curse, spoken as a wish
decisions.reason: The verb is a wish or command in form. It takes effect at once.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: to find some figs; will (for may)
decisions.reason: Readable says why Jesus went to the tree, as 21:18 implies, and gives the curse as a firm statement.

source.text: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες· Πῶς παραχρῆμα ἐξηράνθη ἡ συκῆ;

records.literal_gloss: And having seen the disciples marveled saying, How immediately withered the fig tree?

en.L: And when the disciples saw [it], they marveled, saying, "How did the fig tree wither at once?"
en.B: The disciples were astonished when they saw this. "How did the fig tree dry up so quickly?" they asked.
en.R: The followers saw this and were amazed. They asked, "How did the fig tree dry up so fast?"

decisions.choice: how so quickly: amazement at the speed
decisions.reason: The disciples ask how it could happen at once, not why Jesus did it.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν καὶ μὴ διακριθῆτε, οὐ μόνον τὸ τῆς συκῆς ποιήσετε, ἀλλὰ κἂν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ εἴπητε· Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, γενήσεται·

records.literal_gloss: Answering then the Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you, if you have faith and not doubt, not only the of the fig tree you will do, but even if to the mountain this you say, Be taken up and be cast into the sea, it will happen;

en.L: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what [was done to] the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will happen.
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will do more than what was done to this fig tree. Even if you tell this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will be done.
en.R: Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth. If you have faith and do not doubt, you will be able to do what was done to this fig tree. And you will do even more. You could say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' and it would happen.

decisions.choice: faith and not doubting: trust in God that does not waver
decisions.reason: To doubt is to be divided, wavering between trust and distrust. Jesus spoke of faith that moves a mountain in 17:20 too.

decisions.choice: moving a mountain: doing what seems impossible
alternatives: a literal plan to move hills
decisions.reason: Removing mountains was a picture of the impossible (Isaiah 40:4; Zechariah 4:7). Jesus speaks with the same picture in 17:20.

decisions.choice: this mountain: probably the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: They are walking from Bethany over the Mount of Olives to the city. From there the Dead Sea can be seen. Some see the temple mount meant.

decisions.choice: be lifted up and thrown: God is the one who acts
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed; it is God who answers faith.

decisions.choice: the fig tree first, then even more
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long comparison into short sentences.

source.text: καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ πιστεύοντες λήμψεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: And all things as many as if you ask in the prayer believing you will receive.

en.L: And all things whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive."
en.B: And everything you ask for in prayer you will receive, as long as you believe."
en.R: When you pray and believe, you will receive anything you ask for."

decisions.choice: whatever you ask, believing: prayer that trusts God the Father
alternatives: a promise to grant any wish
decisions.reason: Jesus has taught his disciples to pray for God's will to be done (6:10) and promised that the Father gives good things (7:11). The promise is made to that kind of trust.

decisions.choice: believing: the condition under which they ask
decisions.reason: The participle describes the asking: those who ask while trusting God.

source.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ διδάσκοντι οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ λέγοντες· Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: And having come of him into the temple came to him teaching the chief priests and the elders of the people saying, By what authority these things are you doing?

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching, saying, "By what authority are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} doing these things?
en.B: Jesus went into the temple courts, and while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching, the chief priests and the elders of the people came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "What authority do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have for doing these things?" they asked.
en.R: Jesus went into the temple area and began to teach. The leading priests and the older leaders of the people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They asked, "What right do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have to do these things?

decisions.choice: the chief priests and the elders of the people: the leaders of the temple and the nation
decisions.reason: The chief priests ran the temple, and the elders were heads of leading families. With the scribes they made up the council (16:21).

decisions.choice: these things: his entry, the clearing of the temple, his healing and teaching there
decisions.reason: The leaders ask who gave him the right to act as he has in the temple since 21:12.

decisions.choice: authority: the right to act, given by someone
decisions.reason: The question is who gave Jesus the right, as the next sentence makes plain.

decisions.choice: the question closes this sentence; the second question follows
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "they asked" after the first question, and the next record gives the second.

decisions.choice: right
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for the right to act.

source.text: καὶ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;

records.literal_gloss: And who to you gave the authority this?

en.L: And who gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} this authority?"
en.B: "And who gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} this authority?"
en.R: Who gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} this right?"

decisions.choice: who gave you: the second question presses the first
decisions.reason: The leaders want Jesus to name the source of his authority, which they claim to control in the temple.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον ἕνα, ὃν ἐὰν εἴπητέ μοι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν ἐρῶ ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ·

records.literal_gloss: Answering then the Jesus said to them, Will ask you I also word one, which if you tell me, I also to you will say by what authority these things I do;

en.L: And answering, Jesus said to them, "I also will ask you one question; if you tell {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [the answer], I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.
en.B: Jesus replied, "I too will put one question to you. If you answer it for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, then I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
en.R: Jesus answered, "I will ask you one question too. If you answer it, I will tell you what right I have to do these things.

decisions.choice: a question in return: a usual way of debate among teachers
decisions.reason: Answering a question with a question was a common way for teachers to argue. Jesus will answer if they do.

decisions.choice: word: here a question
decisions.reason: The noun has a wide range; the verb "ask" shows it means one question.

source.text: τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ Ἰωάννου πόθεν ἦν;

records.literal_gloss: The baptism the of John from where was it?

en.L: The baptism of John, where was it from?
en.B: John's baptism, where did it come from?
en.R: Where did John's right to baptize come from?

decisions.choice: the baptism of John: his whole call to repent and be baptized
decisions.reason: John's baptism stands for his work as a prophet (3:1-12). The question is whether God sent him.

source.text: ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;

records.literal_gloss: From heaven or from men?

en.L: From heaven or from {{gender:people|men}}?"
en.B: Was it from heaven or from human beings?"
en.R: Did it come from God in heaven? Or did it come from people?"

decisions.choice: from heaven: from God
decisions.reason: Speaking of heaven was a reverent way to speak of God, as in "the kingdom of heaven".

decisions.choice: God in heaven
decisions.reason: Readable says that heaven stands for God.

source.text: οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες· Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ ἡμῖν· Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;

records.literal_gloss: They then were reasoning among themselves saying, If we say, From heaven, he will say to us, Why then not did you believe him?

en.L: And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
en.B: They began to argue it out among themselves: "If we say, 'From heaven,' {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will ask us, 'Then why did you not believe John?'
en.R: The leaders talked about this among themselves. They said, "If we answer, 'From God in heaven,' Jesus will ask us, 'Then why did you not believe John?'

decisions.choice: reasoning among themselves: discussing it with one another
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean thinking within oneself, but they reason together as a group here.

decisions.choice: believe him: accept John's message as from God
alternatives: trust in John as a savior
decisions.reason: To believe John is to accept what he said, including what he said about the one coming after him (3:11).

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom they did not believe.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων, φοβούμεθα τὸν ὄχλον, πάντες γὰρ ὡς προφήτην ἔχουσιν τὸν Ἰωάννην.

records.literal_gloss: If but we say, From men, we fear the crowd, all for as a prophet hold the John.

en.L: But if we say, 'From {{gender:people|men}},' we fear the crowd, for all hold John as a prophet."
en.B: But if we say, 'From human beings,' we have the crowd to fear, since they all regard John as a prophet."
en.R: But if we answer, 'From people,' then we have to worry about the crowd. Everyone thinks John was a prophet."

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off: fear takes the place of the result
decisions.reason: They do not finish the thought "if we say this, then ...". They name their fear instead.

decisions.choice: they all hold John as a prophet: the people's high regard for John
decisions.reason: Crowds from all Judea had gone out to John (3:5). Jesus himself called him a prophet and more (11:9).

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπαν· Οὐκ οἴδαμεν.

records.literal_gloss: And answering Jesus they said, Not we know.

en.L: And answering Jesus, they said, "We do not know."
en.B: So they answered Jesus, "We do not know."
en.R: So they answered Jesus, "We do not know."

decisions.choice: we do not know: a refusal to answer
alternatives: a real admission that they did not know
decisions.reason: Their reasoning in 21:25-26 shows that they choose not to commit themselves.

source.text: ἔφη αὐτοῖς καὶ αὐτός· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.

records.literal_gloss: Said to them also he, Neither I tell you by what authority these things I do.

en.L: He also said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Then I will not tell you either by what authority I do these things.
en.R: Jesus said, "Then I will not tell you either what right I have to do these things.

decisions.choice: neither do I tell you: Jesus will not answer those who will not answer
decisions.reason: Jesus keeps the bargain of 21:24. The parables that follow still show where he stands.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

source.text: Τί δὲ ὑμῖν δοκεῖ;

records.literal_gloss: What but to you seems?

en.L: But what do you think?
en.B: Now tell me what you think.
en.R: What do you think about this?

decisions.choice: what do you think: an invitation to judge the story
decisions.reason: Jesus asks his hearers to give a verdict, as he does in 18:12 and 22:42. Their answer will judge them (21:31).

source.text: ἄνθρωπος εἶχεν τέκνα δύο.

records.literal_gloss: A man had children two.

en.L: A man had two children.
en.B: A man had two sons.
en.R: There was a man who had two sons.

decisions.choice: children: here two sons
decisions.reason: The word means children, but the forms in 21:29-30 show both are sons.

decisions.choice: children (L); sons (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the general word; Balanced and Readable say what the story shows.

decisions.choice: no spans for the father
alternatives: spans on he and his for the father
decisions.reason: The father is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no deity_pronoun span.

source.text: προσελθὼν τῷ πρώτῳ εἶπεν· Τέκνον, ὕπαγε σήμερον ἐργάζου ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι.

records.literal_gloss: Having come to the first he said, Child, go today work in the vineyard.

en.L: Coming to the first, he said, 'Child, go today, work in the vineyard.'
en.B: He came to the first one and said, 'Go and work in the vineyard today, son.'
en.R: The father went to the first son and said, 'Son, go and work in the vineyard today.'

decisions.choice: child: a father's warm address to his son
decisions.reason: The word is used as a kindly address (9:2).

decisions.choice: the vineyard: a familiar picture of God's people and his work
decisions.reason: Israel is God's vineyard in Isaiah 5:1-7, and 20:1-16 pictured work in a vineyard. The picture returns in 21:33.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐ θέλω· ὕστερον δὲ μεταμεληθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: He then answering said, Not I want; later then having regretted he went.

en.L: And answering, he said, 'I do not want to'; but later, having changed his mind, he went.
en.B: He answered, 'I do not want to.' Yet afterward he changed his mind and went.
en.R: The son answered, 'I will not go.' But later he was sorry. He changed his mind and went to work.

decisions.choice: the first son refuses and then goes; the second agrees and does not go: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the order reversed, with the first son agreeing and not going, and the answer "the last" in 21:31
the order of the SBLGNT, but with the answer "the last"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts tell this parable in three forms. Some important early ones reverse the two sons and have the answer "the last". A few others keep this order but give the answer "the last", which makes the leaders answer wrongly. The meaning of the parable is the same in the first two forms. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: changed his mind: regretted his answer and turned around
decisions.reason: The verb means to regret and change course. Jesus uses it again in 21:32 of those who did not change their minds and believe.

decisions.choice: he was sorry. He changed his mind
decisions.reason: Readable gives both sides of the verb: regret and a change of course.

source.text: προσελθὼν δὲ τῷ δευτέρῳ εἶπεν ὡσαύτως· ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἐγώ, κύριε· καὶ οὐκ ἀπῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: Having come then to the second he said likewise. He then answering said, I, sir; and not he went.

en.L: And coming to the second, he said the same. And answering, he said, 'I [go], sir,' and he did not go.
en.B: Then the father went to the second son and said the same thing. This one answered, 'I will, sir,' but he did not go.
en.R: Then the father went to the other son and told him the same thing. This son answered, 'Yes, sir, I will go.' But he did not go.

decisions.choice: I, sir: a short and polite yes, with the verb understood
decisions.reason: The reply has only "I" and the address. It means "I will go, sir".

decisions.choice: sir: the respectful address to a father or master
alternatives: Lord, as an address to God
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the Lord; here it is a son's respectful word to his father.

decisions.choice: the father; son
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who spoke to whom.

source.text: τίς ἐκ τῶν δύο ἐποίησεν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός;

records.literal_gloss: Which of the two did the will of the father?

en.L: Which of the two did the will of the father?"
en.B: Which of the two did what their father wanted?"
en.R: Which of the two sons did what his father wanted?"

decisions.choice: doing the will of the father: the test Jesus gave in 7:21
alternatives: only a son's duty at home
decisions.reason: Not everyone who says "Lord" will enter the kingdom, but the one who does the will of the Father (7:21; 12:50).

decisions.choice: did what their father wanted (B); did what his father wanted (R)
alternatives: did the will of the father
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the phrase in plain words.

source.text: λέγουσιν· Ὁ πρῶτος.

records.literal_gloss: They say, The first.

en.L: They say, "The first."
en.B: "The first," they answered.
en.R: They answered, "The first son."

decisions.choice: the first, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the last, in manuscripts that reverse the sons
the last, in a few manuscripts that keep this order
decisions.reason: See the note on 21:29. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι προάγουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Jesus, Truly I say to you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes go before you into the kingdom of the God.

en.L: Jesus says to them, "Truly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God.
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are leading the way into the kingdom of God, ahead of you.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth. Tax collectors and prostitutes are going into God's kingdom before you.

decisions.choice: are going ahead of you: they enter first, and the leaders have not yet entered
decisions.reason: The verb means to go before someone. It leaves the door open for the leaders, though 21:43 warns that the kingdom will be taken from them.

decisions.choice: tax collectors and prostitutes: people the devout counted as beyond hope
decisions.reason: Tax collectors worked for the rulers and were known for cheating (9:10-11). Prostitutes lived plainly against the law. Both are named as those who believed John (21:32).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable uses the shorter form, as in 4:23.

source.text: ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ὁδῷ δικαιοσύνης, καὶ οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ· οἱ δὲ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι ἐπίστευσαν αὐτῷ· ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰδόντες οὐδὲ μετεμελήθητε ὕστερον τοῦ πιστεῦσαι αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Came for John to you in way of righteousness, and not you believed him; the but tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; you but having seen not even regretted afterward to believe him.

en.L: For John came to you in [the] way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and you, having seen [it], did not even change your minds afterward to believe him.
en.B: For John came to you showing the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and the prostitutes did believe him. And even after you saw that, you did not change your minds later and believe him.
en.R: John came to show you the righteous way to live, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. You saw this happen. But even then you did not change your minds and believe him.

decisions.choice: in the way of righteousness: living and teaching the right way before God
alternatives: only in a righteous manner of life
decisions.reason: John both lived rightly and called people to the life God requires (3:2-12). Jesus said that he and John were to fulfill all righteousness (3:15).

decisions.choice: change your minds: the same verb as the first son's change in 21:29
alternatives: repent of all sin in general
decisions.reason: The leaders are like the second son. They said yes to God but did not turn when John came, even when they saw sinners turn.

decisions.choice: to believe him: the change they did not make was believing
decisions.reason: The infinitive tells what changing their minds would have meant: coming to believe John.

decisions.choice: the righteous way to live
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key word in its adjective form and says what the way was.
